title: Solve it: allow unless blocked
idea: GUIDED. One problem through UEPCC using 'not' to flip a condition: act unless something is true.
problem: A user may post unless their account is banned. Given is_banned, print 'Allowed' or 'Blocked'.

exercises.prompt:
PROBLEM: May post UNLESS banned. Print 'Allowed' or 'Blocked'.

What is the OUTPUT?
exercises.explanation: One of two labels. 'is_banned' is the input; the label is the output.

exercises.prompt: 'May post unless banned' means posting is allowed when...
exercises.explanation: 'Unless banned' is the same as 'when not banned'. That word 'not' is the clue to the tool.

exercises.prompt: By hand: is_banned is False. Allowed or Blocked?
exercises.explanation: Not banned, so posting is Allowed. 'not False' is True, so the allow branch runs.

exercises.prompt: By hand: is_banned is True. Allowed or Blocked?
exercises.explanation: Banned, so 'not True' is False and the else runs: 'Blocked'.

exercises.prompt: Plan: which tool turns 'is_banned' into 'is not banned'?
exercises.explanation: 'not' flips a true/false value. 'not is_banned' is True exactly when the account is not banned.

exercises.prompt: 'if not is_banned:' runs its body when the account is NOT banned.
exercises.explanation: Yes. 'not' flips the value, so the body runs when is_banned is False.
'not is_banned' is the allow test; the else blocks the banned case.
'not' flips is_banned so the allow branch runs when the account is not banned.

exercises.prompt: Check the first example: is_banned False. What prints?
exercises.explanation: not False is True, so 'Allowed' - matching your hand answer.

exercises.prompt: Fresh case: is_banned True. What prints?
exercises.explanation: not True is False, so the else runs: 'Blocked'. The 'not' correctly flips both cases.
